title: Electrostatics: fields, matter, interfaces and inference
summary: A source-qualified route from Coulomb fields and boundary-value uniqueness to nonlinear dielectrics, correlated electrolytes, quantum interfaces, fluctuation forces and inverse metrology.
scope: Selected foundations and current primary literature; static and quasistatic models retain their distinct domains. Research-line mapping is broader than actual source reading. No exhaustive frontier survey, hardware validation or unique frequency inference is claimed.

formulas.title: Coulomb force with an oriented separation
formulas.plain: The force on charge1 points from2 to1 for like signs.
conditions: Stationary point charges in vacuum, distinct positions; microscopic linear superposition.
derivation: Spherical symmetry fixes a radial field.
Gauss flux fixes its coefficient; multiply the field of2 by q1.
limitingCases: Force vanishes when either charge is zero; doubles if one charge doubles.
pitfalls: The r→0 singularity is not a finite-size charge or contact-force model.

formulas.title: Electric field as a linear source map
formulas.latex: \mathbf E(\mathbf r)=\frac1{4\pi\epsilon_0}\int\rho(\mathbf r\prime)\frac{\mathbf r-\mathbf r\prime}{|\mathbf r-\mathbf r\prime|^3}\,d^3r\prime
formulas.plain: Integrate vector contributions, not field magnitudes.
conditions: Localized integrable source in unbounded vacuum; singular sources need distributions or a prescribed principal value.
derivation: Replace a charge by rho*dV.
Add oriented Coulomb contributions and pass to the continuum integral.

workedExample.inputs: Two equal charges at±a; observe the midpoint
steps: Pair each vector with its opposite.
workedExample.result: E=0 by symmetry despite a nonzero potential.

limitingCases: Far from a localized distribution, its net charge gives the leading field.
pitfalls: Zero field at one point does not imply no charge or zero field energy.

formulas.title: Gauss law and what flux measures
formulas.plain: Flux depends on enclosed total charge; solving for local field additionally needs symmetry.
conditions: Closed oriented surface; microscopic vacuum form includes bound as well as free charge.
derivation: Integrate the inverse-square field over solid angle.
Use superposition or the divergence theorem to obtain divE=rho/epsilon0.
limitingCases: A charge outside contributes zero net flux, but generally nonzero local field.
pitfalls: Replacing E by a uniform magnitude on an arbitrary Gaussian surface is unjustified.

formulas.title: Potential, gauge and path independence
formulas.plain: A potential difference is work per unit positive test charge with the stated minus sign.
conditions: Electrostatic curlE=0 on a simply connected domain, or a globally defined conservative field.
derivation: Apply Stokes theorem to zero curl.
Define phi relative to one reference; adding a constant leaves E unchanged.

workedExample.inputs: Uniform E=100V/m along+x; B lies0.02m aboveA in x

limitingCases: A closed-loop integral is zero in electrostatics.
pitfalls: Time-varying magnetic flux can make the electric field nonconservative; a scalar potential alone then fails.

formulas.title: Heterogeneous-permittivity Poisson equation
formulas.plain: Free charge, constitutive response and boundary data determine the potential together.
conditions: Local linear dielectric; tensor bounded and coercive; suitable Dirichlet/Neumann data.
derivation: Combine D=epsilonE, E=−gradphi and divD=rho_f.
Do not move spatially varying epsilon outside the divergence.

workedExample.inputs: 1D slab with constant epsilon and uniform rho; phi(0)=phi(L)=0

limitingCases: For constant scalar epsilon this becomes −epsilon*Laplacian(phi)=rho_f.
pitfalls: Using epsilon*Laplacian(phi) across a jump erases the interface condition.

formulas.title: Laplace uniqueness and the missing constant
formulas.plain: Two solutions with identical admissible data differ only by a gauge constant; Dirichlet data fixes it.

variables.meaning: electrostatic potential in displayed Laplace equation

conditions: Connected bounded Lipschitz domain; real scalar epsilon uniformly positive. The displayed Laplace equation assumes spatially constant epsilon; heterogeneous epsilon uses the divergence-form operator of es-f05.

Compare potentials with the same sources and admissible boundary traces. A Dirichlet set of positive measure fixes the gauge; all-Neumann data require compatibility and a specified additive constant/mean. Disconnected regions need these conditions componentwise.
derivation: Subtract the PDEs.
Multiply by the difference and integrate by parts; boundary terms vanish.
Positive epsilon forces equal gradients.

steps: Both phi=0 and phi=7V solve the same gradient problem.
workedExample.result: Only the additive constant is undetermined.

limitingCases: With two fixed endpoint voltages in1D, phi is their linear interpolation.
pitfalls: All-Neumann solvability also needs total-charge/flux compatibility, not just a numerical gauge.

formulas.title: Electrostatic interface conditions
formulas.latex: \mathbf n\cdot(\mathbf D_2-\mathbf D_1)=\sigma_f,\qquad\mathbf n\times(\mathbf E_2-\mathbf E_1)=0
formulas.plain: The normal points from medium1 to2; a free surface sheet jumps normal D, not generically normal E.
conditions: Ideal zero-thickness interface without a prescribed dipole-sheet potential jump; static fields.
derivation: Shrink a Gaussian pillbox to the interface.
Shrink a rectangular Faraday loop to obtain tangential continuity.

workedExample.inputs: No free sheet; epsilon2=2epsilon1; field normal

limitingCases: Equal permittivities and zero sheet give continuous E.
pitfalls: A conducting surface may carry induced free charge; setting sigma_f=0 there is usually wrong.

formulas.title: Localized-source far-field expansion
formulas.latex: \phi(\mathbf r)=\frac1{4\pi\epsilon_0}\left(\frac Qr+\frac{\mathbf p\cdot\widehat{\mathbf r}}{r^2}+O(r^{-3})\right),\quad\mathbf p=\int\mathbf r\prime\rho\,dV\prime
formulas.plain: Net charge and dipole moment organize the leading spatial decay.
conditions: Source support lies within radius a and r>a; origin matters when Q is nonzero.
derivation: Expand1/|r−rprime| in rprime/r.
Integrate successive angular moments.

workedExample.inputs: Charges±q separated by d; r≫d on the axis

limitingCases: For Q=0 the dipole may lead; if p also vanishes, higher moments control.
pitfalls: A visually symmetric image is not a measured charge distribution or a justified multipole truncation.

formulas.title: Dipole energy and a nonuniform field force
formulas.latex: U=-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf E,\quad\boldsymbol\tau=\mathbf p\times\mathbf E,\quad\mathbf F=\nabla(\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf E)
formulas.plain: Orientation energy and translation force are different consequences of an imposed field.
conditions: Small fixed dipole, field varies slowly across it; no induced-dipole factor or self-field included.
derivation: Sum forces and work on the two opposite charges.
Retain the first order in separation.

steps: The cross product vanishes and the gradient is zero.

limitingCases: A uniform field can rotate a misaligned dipole without translating it.
pitfalls: For a linearly induced dipole p=alphaE, its charging energy has a factor1/2.

formulas.title: Capacitance and the parallel-plate approximation
formulas.plain: Capacitance is a geometry/material/boundary response, not charge stored without a voltage reference.
conditions: Linear dielectric; d much smaller than lateral electrode size; opposing charges and negligible fringing.
derivation: Gauss law gives E≈Q/(epsilonA).
Integrate DeltaV≈Ed and divide Q by voltage.
limitingCases: C doubles with area and halves with gap in this limit.
pitfalls: Small or edge-dominated electrodes require a field solution; measured parasitics add capacitance.

formulas.title: Maxwell capacitance matrix
formulas.latex: Q_i=\sum_j C_{ij}V_j,\qquad U=\tfrac12\mathbf V^T\mathbf C\mathbf V
formulas.plain: A multi-electrode system needs an explicitly grounded reference or a retained gauge mode.
conditions: Linear reciprocal electrostatics with fixed conductor geometry; the full isolated matrix is gauge singular.
derivation: Linearity lets each electrode basis voltage define a response column.
Reciprocity gives symmetry; integrate charging work.

workedExample.inputs: Two isolated conductors with mutual capacitance C
workedExample.result: Adding the same voltage to both leaves charges unchanged.

limitingCases: After grounding one electrode the remaining matrix is positive on allowed voltages.
pitfalls: Circuit mutual capacitances and off-diagonal Maxwell coefficients differ in sign convention.

formulas.title: Stored field energy and nonlinear qualification
formulas.latex: U=\tfrac12\int\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf D\,dV;\qquad w(\mathbf D)=\int_0^{\mathbf D}\mathbf E(\mathbf D\prime)\cdot d\mathbf D\prime
formulas.plain: The one-half expression requires a linear reversible constitutive relation; nonlinear work needs the constitutive path.
conditions: Lossless reversible local medium; fixed mechanical state. First equality applies only to linear D(E).
derivation: Charge the system quasistatically: incremental work is E·dD.
Integrate along the reversible constitutive curve.
limitingCases: At zero field a reference with zero remanent energy can be assigned U=0.
pitfalls: Ferroelectric hysteresis, losses and electrostriction cannot be hidden inside a constant epsilon.

formulas.title: Force at fixed voltage versus fixed charge
formulas.plain: The voltage source changes the appropriate thermodynamic potential; differentiating field energy at fixed V alone gives the wrong sign.

variables.meaning: voltage-controlled electric thermodynamic potential including source work
stored field energy Q²/(2C)=CV²/2 at the specified state
constant dielectric permittivity in the plate example
overlap area in the plate example

conditions: Quasistatic linear capacitor; mechanical coordinate and controlled electrical ensemble explicitly fixed.
derivation: At fixed Q, force is minus the x derivative of U=Q²/(2C).
At fixed V, source work is deltaW_source=V*deltaQ. Legendre transform G=U−VQ=−CV²/2; F=−partialG/partialx at fixed V.
Differentiate the controlled potential, not field energy with the source omitted.

workedExample.inputs: x is plate separation and C=epsilonA/x

limitingCases: At V=0 with no trapped charge, this ideal force vanishes.
pitfalls: A power supply is an energy port; electrostatic attraction does not create energy.
Changing the plate gap at fixed V returns or draws charge through the supply; electrical source work and external mechanical work must both appear in the energy balance.

formulas.title: Maxwell stress in a simple dielectric
formulas.plain: Stress converts a solved field to a force under a declared material-mechanics model.
conditions: Static, homogeneous isotropic medium or vacuum integration surface; mechanical/electrostrictive terms must be handled consistently in matter.
derivation: Balance momentum across a surface.
The normal field produces pressure epsilonE²/2 on an ideal conductor.

workedExample.inputs: Vacuum E=1e5V/m normal to a conductor

limitingCases: For zero field this field-only stress vanishes.
pitfalls: Applying the vacuum expression inside a deformable nonlinear dielectric can omit material stresses.

formulas.title: Polarization and electric displacement
formulas.plain: D packages free-charge bookkeeping; P records dipole moment per volume.
conditions: Second relation assumes local linear isotropic response without remanence; first is the standard macroscopic definition.
derivation: Coarse-grain microscopic dipoles.
Separate imposed/free charge from bound polarization charge.
limitingCases: Vacuum has P=0 and D=epsilon0E.
pitfalls: D is not universally the physical microscopic field and need not be continuous normally.

formulas.title: Bound volume and surface charge
formulas.plain: A polarized body may have no volume charge and still carry opposite bound surface sheets.
conditions: Macroscopic polarization with resolved boundary; discontinuities can be represented distributionally.
derivation: Integrate dipole charge over a small volume.
Apply the divergence theorem to transfer termination of P to the surface.

steps: divP=0 in the interior; top/bottom normals reverse.
workedExample.result: Surface sheets+P0 and−P0; no bulk rho_b.

limitingCases: A uniform polarization in an infinite periodic model has no physical outer surface.
pitfalls: Do not add sigma_b twice when using an epsilon-based interface formulation.

formulas.title: Anisotropic electrostatic energy
formulas.plain: Anisotropy changes direction as well as magnitude; a stable reciprocal dielectric has positive quadratic energy.
conditions: Real symmetric positive-definite tensor in a local quasistatic reciprocal model.
derivation: Differentiate the quadratic energy with respect to E.
Diagonalize the tensor along principal axes.

workedExample.result: D is not parallel to E; w=3epsilon0E0².

limitingCases: Scalar epsilon is the isotropic special case.
pitfalls: A frequency-dependent negative real permittivity requires dispersive energy; this static positive-energy model is not applicable.

formulas.title: Clausius–Mossotti local-field model
formulas.plain: A molecular polarizability becomes a bulk response only after a local-field hypothesis.
conditions: Isotropic weakly interacting polarizable units with Lorentz spherical-cavity local field; no strong correlations or permanent-dipole complications.
derivation: Use E_local=E+P/(3epsilon0).
Substitute P=n*alpha_m*E_local and solve for susceptibility.
limitingCases: At dilute n, chi_e≈nalpha_m/epsilon0.
pitfalls: The apparent denominator singularity signals model breakdown, not a universal ferroelectric transition prediction.

formulas.title: Planar dielectric image charge
formulas.plain: An image is an auxiliary mathematical charge reproducing boundary data on one side.
conditions: Infinite planar interface, linear isotropic homogeneous half-spaces, no prescribed free sheet; qprime is used for the medium1 potential.
derivation: Write real+image Green functions.
Match tangential E and normal D at the plane.
limitingCases: Equal media give no image; conductor limit epsilon2→infinity gives−q.
pitfalls: The image is not a second physical source; evaluating self-force must exclude the real charge singularity.

formulas.title: Landau differential stability
formulas.plain: A homogeneous stationary branch is not necessarily a stable state.
conditions: Phenomenological homogeneous mean-field expansion; stability requires second derivative positive with the controlled ensemble and any circuit/domain terms included.

The stationary/curvature conditions are local. Global equilibrium requires comparing admissible minima and nonuniform/domain states; if treating the polynomial globally, its highest retained even-power coefficient must make it bounded below.
derivation: Set derivative of f with respect to P to zero.
Differentiate E(P): slope=a+3bP²+5cP⁴.

workedExample.result: P=E/a is a stable linear branch.

limitingCases: If a<0,b>0 at E=0, P=0 is unstable and nonzero minima appear.
pitfalls: Domain walls, gradients, strain and switching kinetics are omitted; fitted coefficients are not universal constants.

formulas.title: Series stabilization and negative differential capacitance
formulas.plain: A negative subsystem slope can coexist with a positive total curvature under constrained coupling.
conditions: Same incremental charge in a series quasistatic model; total free-energy curvature positive; leakage and domain alternatives must be checked.
derivation: Sum incremental voltages dV=dQ/Cs+dQ/Cf.
Positive dV/dQ is the local total-system stability requirement.

workedExample.result: Ctot=2nF; if Cf=−.5nF the total curvature is negative.

limitingCases: Cf→infinity leaves Ctot=Cs.
pitfalls: A transient negative dQ/dV trace alone does not demonstrate stable equilibrium negative capacitance or energy creation.

formulas.title: Boltzmann ion distribution
formulas.plain: Equilibrium ion density follows a balance of ideal mixing entropy and electrostatic energy.
conditions: Dilute ideal ions at thermal equilibrium, uniform temperature, reservoir chemical potentials and point-ion mean field.
derivation: Set mu_i=kBT*ln(n_i)+z_i*e*psi+constant equal to its reservoir value.
Exponentiate.
limitingCases: At psi=0 the reservoir concentration is recovered.
pitfalls: Divergent accumulation at a highly charged wall is a point-ion model failure.

formulas.title: Nonlinear Poisson–Boltzmann equation
formulas.plain: The electrostatic field and ion distribution must be solved self-consistently.
conditions: Mean-field point ions, local continuum dielectric, equilibrium reservoir and specified wall conditions; reservoir electroneutrality is required.
derivation: Insert ideal Boltzmann densities into Poisson.
For symmetric1:1 salt the mobile charge is−2en_b*sinh(epsi/kBT).

workedExample.inputs: Neutral homogeneous reservoir with no fixed charge
steps: Choose psi=0 and equal cation/anion densities.
workedExample.result: Both sides vanish; psi=0 is a solution.

limitingCases: Linearization gives Debye–Hückel only for small dimensionless potential.
pitfalls: Mean-field PB neglects ion correlations, finite size, hydration and image self-energy unless extended.

formulas.title: Debye screening length
formulas.plain: Screening length depends on ionic strength, dielectric response and temperature, not charge signs alone.
conditions: Linearized dilute PB in a uniform bulk electrolyte; concentrations converted to number density.
derivation: Expand exp(−zi*u) to first order.
The zeroth-order charge cancels by electroneutrality; remaining coefficient is kappa².
limitingCases: Increasing concentration100-fold reduces lambdaD tenfold in this model.
pitfalls: Molarity is mol/L; inserting1mM as0.001mol/m³ gives a spurious factor sqrt1000.

formulas.title: Screened point-charge Green function
formulas.plain: A Yukawa form is a linear-response Green function, not the exact nonlinear field near a highly charged ion.
conditions: Unbounded homogeneous linearized electrolyte; small perturbation away from the source core.
derivation: Solve (−Laplacian+kappa²)psi=qdelta/epsilon.
Spherical decay and the Coulomb singular flux fix the coefficient.

workedExample.result: Potential is0.368 of the corresponding unscreened value.

limitingCases: kappa→0 restores the Coulomb potential.
pitfalls: A fitted decay length in concentrated solutions need not equal the dilute Debye length.

formulas.title: Planar Grahame relation
formulas.plain: For a planar symmetric monovalent diffuse layer, surface charge and potential are nonlinearly related.

variables.meaning: bulk density of each salt species

conditions: Single infinite planar surface,1:1 PB electrolyte, no Stern layer or correlations, vanishing bulk potential/field. Positive psi0 corresponds to positive sigma.
derivation: Multiply the1D PB equation by psi prime.
Integrate once using the bulk boundary condition, then use normal Gauss law.
limitingCases: At psi0=0 the charge is zero.
pitfalls: Curvature, finite ion size and compact-layer voltage invalidate direct use as an electrode-total capacitance.

formulas.title: A lattice-gas crowding correction
formulas.plain: A finite site volume prevents point-ion density divergence within one explicit modified mean-field model.
conditions: Equal-size symmetric ions with lattice-gas entropy, bulk volume fraction2vn_b<1; mean field still neglects electrostatic correlations.
derivation: Include the solvent-vacancy entropy in chemical potentials.
Solve their equilibrium ratios under site exclusion.
limitingCases: v→0 recovers ideal Boltzmann densities.
pitfalls: A hard density cap is not a quantitative theory of hydration, asymmetric ions or oscillatory packing layers.

formulas.title: Bjerrum length and planar coupling parameter
formulas.plain: Thermal energy versus Coulomb energy and interfacial charge density determine whether independent-ion intuition is credible.

variables.meaning: Gouy–Chapman wall length under this valence/surface-charge convention

conditions: Xi convention is for a planar counterion-only charged wall; added salt, dielectric images and finite ion sizes require separate parameters.
derivation: Define ellB by setting the unit-charge Coulomb energy at that length equal to kBT.
For a planar wall define muGC=e/(2πz ellB |sigma|); combining z²ellB/muGC gives the displayed Xi.
This is a declared standard-model nondimensionalization, independently reconstructed here, not a theorem attributed to the modern interface/slab papers.

workedExample.result: Xi≈3.2; z=3 gives≈86 under the same convention.

limitingCases: Increasing valence changes Xi cubically in this wall model.
pitfalls: A single Xi threshold does not universally certify mean-field validity for every geometry and salt mixture.
The planar coupling parameter is a declared standard-model definition; the cited current interface/slab papers provide context, not a verified original derivation of this parameter.
Strong coupling between two mechanical modes in the Casimir paper is a different dimensionless comparison from this counterion Xi; matching terminology is not a shared physical mechanism.

formulas.title: Compact and diffuse capacitances in series
formulas.plain: Voltage partition between compact and diffuse layers must be separated before interpreting a measured differential capacitance.
conditions: Uniform planar interface with same incremental charge through both idealized layers; adsorption can introduce additional coupled state variables.
derivation: Write dV=dVS+dVD.
Divide by dSigma and identify the inverse slopes.
limitingCases: The smaller positive capacitance dominates.
pitfalls: A fitted Stern thickness is not necessarily a literal ion diameter or a directly measured molecular boundary.

formulas.title: Acid-site charge regulation
formulas.plain: A surface boundary charge may be an equilibrium unknown rather than a fixed number.

variables.meaning: site equilibrium constant in pH notation

conditions: Independent identical acid sites AH→A−+H+, ideal local proton activity and electrochemical equilibrium; no lateral cooperativity.
derivation: Mass action gives theta/(1−theta)=Ka/aH(surface).
Positive surface potential reduces local proton concentration by exp(−eψ/kBT).
limitingCases: Very low bulk pH protonates the sites under these assumptions.
pitfalls: pH is an activity convention, not simply number density; a sign error reverses the predicted feedback.

formulas.title: Quantum capacitance from compressibility
formulas.plain: Charging a low-density-of-states electron system changes its chemical potential as well as its electrostatic potential.

variables.meaning: density of states per area per joule

conditions: Equilibrium electronic compressibility; integral form assumes an independently specified DOS and no additional self-consistent interaction correction.
derivation: An electrical voltage increment shifts electron electrochemical energy by e*dV.
Differentiate charge density e*n with respect to that increment.

steps: Integrating the normalized Fermi derivative gives1.
workedExample.result: cQ=e²g0, independent of temperature in a broad constant-DOS band.

limitingCases: At zero temperature cQ probes DOS at the chemical potential.
pitfalls: A capacitance fitted from a circuit may also include ions, traps, geometry, kinetics and contacts.

formulas.title: Ideal graphene quantum capacitance
formulas.plain: The clean zero-temperature Dirac model predicts a chemical-potential-dependent electronic capacitance.

variables.meaning: chemical potential measured from Dirac point

conditions: Ideal monolayer graphene with spin/valley degeneracy4, linear dispersion and T=0; disorder/interactions neglected.
derivation: Count2D Dirac states to obtain n=sgn(mu)*mu²/(πhbar²vF²).
Differentiate n with respect to mu and multiply by e².
limitingCases: At ideal T=0 neutrality the formula tends to zero.
pitfalls: Finite temperature and charge puddles smooth the Dirac-point minimum; a real material need not have zero measured capacitance.

formulas.title: Geometric and electronic voltage partition
formulas.plain: Electrochemical charging distributes voltage between the electrostatic gap and electronic compressibility.
conditions: Same incremental areal charge, equilibrium linear response and no unmodeled trap or ionic branch; all areas consistently normalized.
derivation: Total electrochemical voltage is geometric voltage plus chemical-potential change/e.
Differentiate with respect to charge per area.
limitingCases: cQ≫cg recovers the geometric limit.
pitfalls: Negative compressibility can enhance capacitance, but stable total curvature and correct ensemble must still be verified.

formulas.title: Kelvin-probe first-harmonic null
formulas.plain: A force harmonic null estimates a capacitance-weighted contact potential under an instrument model.
conditions: Expand Fz=.5Cprime(z)[Vdc−VCPD+Vac*cos(omega*t)]²; quasistatic capacitive force, fixed tip geometry and uniform effective sample potential.
Coordinate z increases tip–sample separation. With Fz=+Cprime(z)Vgap²/2, Cprime is normally negative for attraction; an opposite coordinate flips force signs but not the null.
derivation: The cross term in squared voltage supplies the omega harmonic.
Its null gives Vdc=VCPD when additional charge forces are absent.

workedExample.result: First harmonic is zero even though DC and2omega forces may remain.

limitingCases: If Vac=0 there is no lock-in harmonic with which to locate the null.
pitfalls: Tip convolution, trapped charge, surface dipoles and feedback dynamics prevent an automatic absolute work-function interpretation.
This first-harmonic identity is derived here from the capacitive-force model; a complete contemporary KPFM instrument review was not performed.
The1991 paper was inspected only through metadata/deposited abstract; do not label this force identity as a checked transcription of that original article.

formulas.title: Thermal charge fluctuations at fixed voltage
formulas.plain: Response and equilibrium noise are linked only within a specified stable ensemble.

variables.meaning: positive differential capacitance at fixed control conditions

conditions: Classical equilibrium, voltage-controlled conjugate ensemble, local convex free energy; low-frequency thermodynamic fluctuations not a full detector noise spectrum.
derivation: Differentiate the voltage-ensemble partition function.
The response derivative equals beta times charge variance.
limitingCases: At strictly fixed total Q that constrained charge has zero ensemble variance.
pitfalls: A negative variance cannot be inferred by substituting an unstable isolated negative capacitance branch.

formulas.title: Electrostatic zero-frequency interaction sector
formulas.plain: This is one classical electrostatic sector of planar fluctuation theory, not the whole retarded quantum Casimir force.

variables.meaning: dimensionless substitution2ka used in the derivation
Riemann zeta value sum of reciprocal positive cubes

conditions: Planar local media with static electric response, equilibrium and specified intervening medium; screening and boundary prescriptions can change the zero mode.
derivation: At zero Matsubara frequency, retain only the static electric/TM sector of the declared planar model. The half-weight zero term times the2D mode measure gives kBT/(4π) times integral k*dk.
Set u=2ka, so k*dk=u*du/(4a²). Expand log(1−exp(−u))=−sum exp(−n*u)/n.
Termwise integration gives integral u*log(1−exp(−u))du=−sum1/n³=−zeta(3); hence one ideal electric sector yields−zeta(3)kBT/(16πa²).

steps: Expand log(1−x) and integrate each exponential term.

limitingCases: If one electric reflection coefficient is zero this sector vanishes.
pitfalls: Adding this term to a full Lifshitz calculation that already includes n=0 double counts it; quantum/retarded sectors are not derived here.
Adding an ideal TE zero mode doubles this term; that is a different magnetic/material boundary prescription, not the single electrostatic sector stated here.

formulas.title: Weak Poisson form with explicit flux sign
formulas.plain: The Neumann variable g is minus the outward displacement flux because E=−gradphi.

variables.meaning: Dirichlet portion where test functions vanish

conditions: Trial potential has specified Dirichlet trace; test functions vanish there; coercivity and integrable sources required.

For the pure-Neumann problem on each connected component, integral rho_f dV + integral g dA=0. Fix the mean or a reference; incompatible data must be rejected rather than hidden by pinning one mesh node.
derivation: Multiply −div(epsilon*gradphi)=rho by v.
Integrate by parts and move the boundary derivative to the right.
limitingCases: For homogeneous Dirichlet data the boundary integral disappears.
pitfalls: Assigning g=D·n reverses the physical sign unless the weak-form convention is changed.

formulas.title: Variational Poisson functional
formulas.plain: Stationarity yields the weak PDE under fixed admissible boundary traces.
conditions: Linear coercive dielectric and fixed sources/boundary controls; gauge fixed for all-Neumann cases.
derivation: Vary phi by a test function.
Set first variation to zero; positivity gives the minimizing solution.

steps: Differentiate J with respect to each coefficient.
workedExample.result: The symmetric stiffness system K*u=f is obtained.

limitingCases: Mesh refinement of a conforming space reduces the functional toward its exact minimum.
pitfalls: This source-loaded PDE functional is not automatically the complete thermodynamic energy of a voltage-controlled mechanical apparatus.

formulas.title: Green boundary representation
formulas.plain: Boundary data can replace a volume discretization in homogeneous regions.
conditions: x strictly inside a smooth bounded homogeneous region; boundary limits require jump terms; kernel solves−LaplacianG=delta.
derivation: Apply Green second identity to phi and G.
Use Poisson and the delta property of G with consistent signs.

workedExample.inputs: Harmonic constant potential V0 inside a sphere
steps: Volume term vanishes; the double-layer integral reproduces the constant.
workedExample.result: Interior phi=V0; evaluating directly on the boundary requires its jump convention.

limitingCases: For a source-free region only boundary terms remain.
pitfalls: Dropping the boundary jump coefficient or using a homogeneous kernel across heterogeneous bulk epsilon gives a wrong integral equation.

formulas.title: Ewald screening split
formulas.plain: An exact algebraic split organizes a long-range periodic sum; it is not by itself the complete periodic energy.
conditions: Identity holds for r>0; full Ewald algorithms additionally require reciprocal terms, self correction, net-charge treatment and a zero-mode/boundary convention.
derivation: Insert erf+erfc=1.
Choose eta so both real and reciprocal representations converge efficiently.
limitingCases: Exact total results must be independent of eta after convergence.
pitfalls: Slab and3D periodic boundaries are different problems; omitting the self term or neutralizing-background convention changes the result.

formulas.title: Tikhonov inverse and a kernel witness
formulas.plain: A regularizer selects a stable estimate under a declared prior; it does not manufacture missing information.

variables.meaning: regularization strength in declared scaled coordinates

conditions: Finite linearized inverse model with consistent nondimensionalization; W positive; combined operator invertible on constrained unknowns.
derivation: Minimize weighted data residual squared plus lambda times penalty squared.
Set its derivative to zero to obtain normal equations.

workedExample.result: x=(1/2,1/2) is a prior-selected representative, not unique recovery from data.

limitingCases: As lambda→0 a unique well-conditioned full-rank inverse is recovered when it exists.
pitfalls: A small residual, positive returned singular values of a rectangular matrix, or a plausible image does not remove an unobserved kernel.

formulas.title: Covariance-aware uncertainty propagation
formulas.plain: A derived result inherits covariance as well as individual input uncertainties.

variables.meaning: input quantities with separately stated units

conditions: Differentiable local measurement model and small enough uncertainties for first-order propagation; coverage probabilities require additional distributional/effective-DOF assumptions.
derivation: Linearize delta y≈sum(Ji*delta xi).
Take its variance, retaining cross terms.

workedExample.inputs: C=Q/V;Q,V have equal1% relative standard uncertainty
steps: For independent errors, add squared sensitivities.
For perfectly common fractional calibration error the correlated terms cancel.
workedExample.result: Independent relative uC≈1.414%; common multiplicative error can cancel exactly in the ratio.

limitingCases: A zero sensitivity suppresses the corresponding first-order contribution, not necessarily higher-order error.
pitfalls: Multiplying by k=2 is not automatically a valid95% interval, and a nonsignificant difference is not equivalence.

sources.claim: Cylindrical ferroelectric/dielectric stacks exhibit geometry-,domain- and charge-compensation-dependent capacitance states in the authors’ experiments and phase-field model.

glossary.definition: International System of Units; all numerical examples convert lengths, charge and energy consistently.
Poisson–Boltzmann, an equilibrium mean-field equation for ideal mobile ions.
Density of electronic states per specified energy and area; units must distinguish joules from electronvolts.
Density-functional theory; here electronic or classical fluid free-energy modeling, not a guarantee of exact material behavior.
Kelvin probe force microscopy; contact-potential inference through a calibrated force/electrostatic transfer model.
Finite-element method; a weak-form discretization with explicit boundary data.
Boundary-element method; integral equations on interfaces with singular-kernel/jump conventions.
An exact long-range splitting plus boundary-dependent periodic summation machinery.
Contact-potential difference; polarity depends on tip/sample voltage convention.
Discrete imaginary-frequency representation of thermal field fluctuations; zero frequency is one sector.
Charge treated as an independently specified mobile or electrode source in the macroscopic constitutive model.
Macroscopic charge associated with the divergence and termination of polarization.
A negative differential voltage/charge slope whose ensemble, dynamics and whole-system stability must be declared.
The electronic compressibility contribution to charging, distinct from geometry and ion adsorption.
An unobservable additive potential constant in electrostatics unless a reference is fixed.
A conclusion requiring a prespecified meaningful margin and statistical/uncertainty procedure, not merely failure to detect a difference.
